I purchased a vehicle on 26th November 2025.  Along with the expensive platinum warranty for 2 years you are highly encouraged to buy....

Within 1 week I was driving the car back...1 hr journey.  All wheels needed balancing, and a tyre completely replaced, along with a new electric window motor for rear drivers passenger.  Yes, 1 hr drive in rain with window open on a motorway.  Yay !!

The response...sorry Zowie you know used cars we can't know these things before you take the car....

All wheels needing to be rebalanced and a new tyre not being picked up before sale.....hmmmm.

Was the car fixed, yes.

Now its April 2026.  Huge issue.

Red warning.  Do not drive car, suspension fault detected.

The vehicle was leaking fluid from nearside rear.  Fluid all over driveway.  Underneath shows a pipe completely saturated.

Message sent to Jack Henry.

' yeah sorry Zowie you know these things happen with used cars, you have your platinum warranty. So youll have to use that.  Get the car recovered....yes thats not covered by your warranty....then see what the garage says and hopefully youll be covered...'

Vehicle purchased Ranger Rover Sport Autobiography £33000 approx.

No. No warranty.

This is a Consumer Rights Act 2015 issue.

I have had various emails with Josh the operations manager.  Who repeatedly tells me to use my warranty.

Citizens Advice and trading standards are now involved.

And Jack Henry are now 1 week into their 14 day notice period.

A vehicle purchased within 6 months under the Consumer Rights Act 2015 must be repaired or replaced by the seller.  At no cost or inconvenience to the customer.  They have 1 attempt at repair to a satisfactory standard.  If not the customer is entitled to a full refund.

I have been told I have been passed to Joshs Manager.

I have not heard from him.

Note to new customers.....

If you buy a car be prepared to buy the warranty, because then they can sell defective cars with no financial comeback.

If you wish to ask me questions  ill be happy to answer.

And once I have received a reply from Jack Henry and a resolution I will happily post it here.
Zowie Carr

Uodate Tuesday 28th April 2026
Yesterday Jack Fowler the MD of Jack Henry Group Ltd began communicating via email.  My car has been collected today at 9.15am by Clint a very pleasant gentleman.

It is being recovered to Jack Henry Groups Service Centre for assessment.  I have been assured it will be repaired and returned at the cost of Jack Henry Group and no longer insisted my warranty be used.

I will update further in due course.

They then messaged me offering £150 towards the cost of my inspection - claiming it wasn't to influence the review - and finally phoned the independent inspector to pressure them into calling me)

I was interested in a Jaguar I-Pace from this dealer. The car had just been put through a fresh MOT by the dealer, which passed with zero advisories, however I was concerned whether track rod ends that had come up in previous advisories had been fixed.

For peace of mind, I paid for an independent inspection.
The inspector's opinion in his report was that the track rod ends did indeed have excessive play, to the degree of being audible inside the car, there were also warning codes from an electronic door handle (though it was functional), severely uneven rear brake wear indicating a binding caliper, and low EV inverter coolant. When I politely raised these documented issues with the sales team to negotiate a repair (I would have happily paid the full price if the issues were resolved) or a realistic discount, they became very defensive, refused to acknowledge the independent inspector's view over their MOT, and offered a token £100 discount.

I decided to walk away. The cars might look great cosmetically, but I always recommend any buyer pays for their own independent mechanical inspection before handing over any money.

Bought a car from James at Pinewood Autos just over a month ago. Whilst everything seemed great at first and service was 5 stars, unfortunately after sales has been a little disappointing.

When viewing the car, the last MOT had an advisory for the rear brakes. I questioned this and asked if this could be sorted prior to purchasing, but was reassured the brakes had plenty of life left and nothing to be concerned about. The seats were also covered in stains but I was told they would ensure everything was cleaned ahead of time.

Proceeded with the purchase of the car, and upon delivery, the brakes were squealing, the passenger and rear washer jet weren’t working, seats were still stained, and the handbrake was loose (10 clicks to even lock out). I emailed James regarding the brakes, washer jets and seats, after a couple of weeks, to make sure no other issues transpired, and was brushed off with ‘it’s just had a service and passed MOT’.

My friend then took it on a little test drive for me to see if there was anything wrong, which is when he pointed out the handbrake was shockingly loose, and agreed with me on the other issues. He then called James for me, and it was only then that any form of resolution was offered. I’m a little unsure why these resolutions were not offered to me to start with. Regardless, I was happy for the assistance and the work was booked in. I was even informed via email that they would go back over the seats whilst my car was booked in.

Upon arrival to get the work conducted yesterday, I was greeted by Katherine, who has been nothing less than superb throughout. She took my car to the garage and we had a lovely chat whilst I waited. Once the work was done, she kindly drove me down the road to collect my car. The work on the handbrake and washer jets had been completed.

On the way home, my car started to have some issues and I unfortunately had to pull over to the side of the m25, however after a couple of minutes and a call with Katherine, she had the guys from the garage come down to meet me, and they were able to resolve the issue for me within an hour, and I was back on my way home. The mechanic did mention how the brakes were absolutely covered in dust, and kindly tried to clean off what he could whilst putting things back together.

Once I got home, I went back through the email chain to thank them for the works completed and mention the brakes, which is when I was reminded they would go back over the seats, which they had failed to do whilst I was there.

I do want to give a special mention to Katherine who, as previously mentioned, has been fantastic help throughout. She was very friendly, helpful, and kept me well informed throughout the repairs yesterday, even offering to drop me off into the local town whilst I waited. A huge thank you to Katherine and her 5 star service!

I have since emailed James but still awaiting a reply. I will update this review once a reply has been received.

4TH MAY UPDATE -

Still no reply from James, and EML came on today! This is now ANOTHER issue and I haven’t even had the car 2 months! I have sent another email with formal rejection of the car. Changed rating to 1 star.

GymBox Bank continues to be a disappointing experience despite charging premium prices. Out of all the GymBox locations across London, Bank is probably one of the better branches, but only because the cost cutting is not as blatantly obvious as it is at some other sites. Overall, GymBox as a brand seems completely focused on reducing costs whilst continuing to charge members premium membership fees.

There have been repeated occasions with no hot water, female sauna not working, poor air conditioning in the female changing rooms and a noticeable build up of mould in the shower areas due to poor ventilation. It is quite concerning, particularly for members with asthma or respiratory concerns.

One of the biggest recurring issues is the complete lack of towels on Monday evenings. GymBox knows full well how busy Mondays are, yet by around 5:30pm there are regularly no towels left. This has happened to me multiple times to the point where I have had to leave and use competitor gyms instead. For a gym open until 11pm, this is simply poor planning and feels like ongoing cost cutting rather than prioritising member experience.

The customer service is also disappointing. Staff are often chatting amongst themselves at reception with little acknowledgement when members arrive and when informing members that there are no towels available, the response can come across dismissive, almost as though it is amusing rather than an inconvenience to paying members.

GymBox needs to stop marketing itself as a premium gym while basic operational standards continue to decline across its London sites. At the very least, ensure there are enough towels available for members throughout the busiest periods of the week.
This place needs to sort out their supply of clean towels before anything better than a one star can be given.

Gymbox time and time again proves to its members that they don't care at all about them or their time, only their money.

Focusing more on trying to look cool on Instagram instead of providing the bare minimum.

The Bank location consistently fails to deliver basic operational standards. Today, I arrived at 09:30 to find the gym completely closed. There was zero communication—no email, no app notification, and not even a sign on the door. This is the second time this month; two weeks ago, I arrived at 11:00 and had to wait outside on the street until they finally decided to open at 12:00, again with absolutely no warning.

Repeatedly leaving members locked outside without explanation shows a complete disregard for our time.

Completely unacceptable service for any price, let alone a 'premium' gym.

I genuinely don’t know how Gymbox still markets itself as a “premium” gym when the experience is closer to a badly managed student union with barbells. Every peak-time visit feels like a cattle market: the place is overcrowded to the point that you’re queuing for dumbbells, fighting for floor space, and trying not to get hit by someone else’s bar because everything is so badly laid out. The constant promos seem designed to ram more people through the door without investing a penny in making the space usable or comfortable for the members already paying full price.

The facilities are a joke for the money they charge. Showers with no hot water, broken or “under repair” machines that stay that way for weeks, saunas out of action for months with zero urgency to fix them – yet they’re more than happy to take full membership fees as if everything is in perfect condition. You pay a premium price and get a half-delivered product, and they don’t even pretend to offer meaningful compensation or a proper apology when key facilities are unavailable.

Customer service manages to be both invisible and hostile at the same time. Staff on-site range from uninterested to outright rude, and when you actually need help, they suddenly become experts in passing you around, stonewalling, or blaming “policy” for everything. The second you raise an issue, it’s like you’ve inconvenienced them by daring to expect basic standards at London’s supposedly “cool” gym.

Where Gymbox really reveals its true colours is with contracts and cancellations. The small-print obsession is unreal: inflexible long contracts, one‑month notice that only runs from the 1st, and a maze of app-based steps and forms just to stop them taking your money. People find themselves chased for months of fees for services they’re not using, threatened with debt collectors over disputed amounts, and told they should have “got it in writing” when staff give wrong information verbally. It feels less like a membership and more like a trap you only realise you’re in once it’s too late.

To top it off, the whole hypey, neon-lit “brand” falls apart the moment you look past the marketing. Classes are impossible to book unless you’re on the app at ridiculous o’clock, and the reality on the gym floor is far from the glossy image they push on social media. If they spent half as much effort on maintenance, member care, and fair policies as they do on pretending to be edgy and premium, they might have a decent product. As it stands, Gymbox is the perfect place if you want to overpay for stress, queues, broken kit and a customer service team that treats you like the problem for daring to complain.

Vanquis Credit Card has completely failed at the most basic level of banking security — and I’m the one paying the price.

I received a message saying my card had been activated.
I had not received the card, not set a PIN, and not authorised anything.

I did the responsible thing — I called them immediately.

Their agent told me: “Don’t worry.”

They did not block the card.

If they had taken basic action and blocked the card at that moment, none of this would have happened.

That advice — and that failure to act — has now led directly to this situation.

A card I never received was somehow activated and used.
No OTP. No verification. No “is this you?” alert. No fraud warning.

Nothing.

Let that sink in — transactions were allowed on a card that was never even in my hands.

I still have no explanation for:

* How the card was activated before delivery
* How a PIN was used when I never set one
* How someone else accessed my details

Instead of stopping this, they sent me a statement saying I owe money.

I have now lost over £1200, and I’m being hit with:

* Arrears
* Interest charges
* Late payment fees
* Risk to my credit history

All for transactions I never authorised.

And it gets worse.

When I contacted them again, I was asked which transactions I wanted to dispute — as if I made any of them.
Then I was told to make minimum payments or my credit file would be affected.

The audacity is unreal.

I asked for a payment hold while they investigate — and they refused.

On top of that, there has been no empathy, no support, no accountability — just rigid, scripted responses focused on payments. The tone felt dismissive and, at times, outright rude.

So let me get this straight:
You were alerted early.
You were contacted.
You had the chance to act.

And you did nothing.

At every step, this bank failed to protect me.

This situation raises serious concerns about how my personal data and identity were handled, as unauthorised access clearly occurred without proper safeguards.

For clarity: under the Payment Services Regulations 2017, customers are not liable for unauthorised transactions unless the bank can prove they were authorised. Yet I am still being pushed to pay interest and charges on a disputed balance.

I reported this early. I trusted what I was told.
And now I’m the one dealing with the damage.

This is not just poor service — this is a complete failure in basic banking security, customer protection, and responsibility.

If this can happen to me, it can happen to anyone.

Think very carefully before trusting this bank with your personal and financial information.

After trading in two vehicles as part of a purchase agreement, the dealer failed to notify the DVLA of the change of keeper. Weeks later, I received official correspondence confirming that I am still recorded as the keeper of both vehicles, which are now showing as untaxed and uninsured — despite the fact that they have been in the dealer’s possession since the day of the trade‑in.

To make matters worse, the dealer karl refused to allow us access to our own V5C documents. We had to repeatedly chase for updates and even return to the showroom in person just to try to get the V5C documents (it appears he has done this multiple times). Despite all of this, the DVLA was still never notified.

This failure has exposed me to potential fines, enforcement action, and legal liability for vehicles I do not own or control. We also have evidence that both vehicles remain on the dealer’s forecourt, making the lack of DVLA notification completely unacceptable. (we have now received fines from the DVLA for both cars and the owner Karl is nowhere to be seen)

Ensuring DVLA updates is a basic legal responsibility for any motor trader. The lack of communication, accountability, and proper administration has caused unnecessary stress, inconvenience and financial penalty. I am now having to escalate the matter to DVLA Enforcement, Trading Standards, and legal advisers.
Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this dealership and would advise anyone to Avoid at all costs.

Looking for a new place to live? Think twice about Rochester Place.

My partner and I moved into a flat in Harringay in September 2024. Our initial interactions with the agency were pleasant, but the experience quickly deteriorated.

When we moved in, the flat had multiple issues including dirty floors, damage to the walls, a dysfunctional kitchen and a broken wardrobe door with a loose glass panel.

A few months later, large areas of black mould began appearing on the walls. We reported it immediately, but were told no tenant had complained in the previous four years and that the issue must be caused by us. Around the same time, I developed ongoing respiratory problems and my GP suggested damp and mould exposure could have been a contributing factor.

We bought an industrial dehumidifier ourselves, which showed humidity levels of 86% and regularly filled its tank twice per day. Despite regular ventilation, recurring leaks in the kitchen and walls that would often “sweat”, the agency continued to insist the issue was our responsibility and refused to bring in a specialist.

It also became clear we were not the only flat affected by damp issues after a neighbour’s bathroom floor partially collapsed due to rot underneath.

Other maintenance problems throughout the tenancy included repeated issues with the shower and a broken oven. In our opinion, repairs were often incomplete or delayed.

Before moving out, we agreed to extend the tenancy slightly while waiting to complete on a property purchase. The agency agreed provided we accepted a £100 rent increase and left a positive Google review, which we never did.

At the end of the tenancy, despite leaving the flat in a much better condition than when we moved in, the agency attempted to deduct money from our deposit for cleaning and mould-related issues. We disputed the deductions through the deposit scheme.

I have rented several flats in London and never previously felt the need to leave a review for an estate agency, but this experience genuinely stood out for the wrong reasons. Based on our experience, I would strongly recommend looking elsewhere.

I would strongly recommend considering alternative parking nearby to avoid the risk of receiving a charge like this.

one_star_reviews.text: Now that we've settled into our home I finally feel ready to review what an awful experience we had with Mowl and Mowl acting as our conveyancing solicitors. We instructed M&M in Sep 25 with Adrian Bowers who was friendly, spoke over the phone, and seemingly was 'getting on with the job'. Unfortunately, our home fell through in Nov 25, but we quickly resold two weeks later to a buyer who had also recently fallen through so was also quite far into the conveyancing process. In Dec 25, we got an out of the blue email to say that Adrian had left the firm and a new solicitor was starting at the end of January but someone was available to deal with enquiries in the mean time. If I could put zero stars I would. Complete scammers. My partner bought a corsa from this garage in February, within 2 weeks we found the EGR was leaking and the tyres were below the legal limit. The owner reluctantly agreed to fix it but put a limit of £150 on repairs, anything more we had to pay towards which we did. We now know this is very much illegal and against consumer rights and his responsibilities as a business. Two weeks after it being fixed the car completely broke down. When we contacted the owner requesting support he was incredibly rude down the phone, he laughed at the suggestion of an exchange, saying he had nothing to exchange for and wouldn’t give us near what we paid for it. When saying he had a responsibility to do something his response was “it’s a second hand car, cars breakdown”. He had no empathy at all. We read up on our rights and returned. Legally he has one opportunity to fix the car without additional cost to us within 6 months, if the car breaks a second time within this period we have the right to a full refund. He did not think these rules applied to him, but eventually offered to attempt to fix the car and if he couldn’t he would refund the price of the car and what we paid towards the repair. After 2 weeks low and behold he could not fix the car, when it came to organising the refund he said he couldn’t give the refund straight away and we would have to wait another week as he didn’t have the money. Instead he tried to offer an exchange for cars he cannot sell and have been sat there for 6 months. This was surprising when he previously laughed at the suggestion of an exchange. We declined the exchange as he had completely lost our trust. Then when collecting the refund he refused to refund the money paid towards the repair as he was refunding the car. My partner owned this car for almost two and a half months and only drove the car for 3-4 weeks. The owner thinks the law doesn’t apply to him and is only out to take advantage of people.

Completely avoid if you want a reliable car and make sure you know your rights! Unfortunately it doesn’t look like we are the first people this has happened to and I doubt we will be the last.

Unfortunately, despite their good reviews, I regret ever using Dacre House Vets. I would caution others against using them.

Unclear prices/lack of transparency:

We initially contacted Dacre House Vets and enquired about some minor dental work for our dog. They estimated a price between £200 and £500, but said it would be at the low end of the scale provided no other issues were found. We registered our dog, and paid £50 for the general check up, prior to booking in the work. Only after this were we given a revised quote of £590 - this is for minor dental work which costs £150 at our new vet. Dacre’s vet's time alone was billed at roughly £200, so Dacre would have always known it would cost in excess of £200 once anaesthetic, etc, was included. Despite this they led us to believe the price would be less, leaving us unable to make an informed decision about registering with them.

They quoted £64 for other, unrelated work. Despite having the quote in writing they charged in excess of this after the treatment was completed. When challenged on this they said the extra charges were for PPE. Again, this is something Dacre would have known they would use, so it should have been included in the original quote.

Inconsistent medical advice:

Dacre advised a medical test was necessary before they or another vet would carry out any dental work on our dog. We paid for this, believing this advice to be accurate. Our current vet has confirmed this was not necessary for the dental work to go ahead.

Lost documents / poor admin:

Our dog is a rescue from overseas. We gave Dacre her passport which contains her medical records shortly after registering with them. We were told they had scanned the information and recorded it.

After moving vets due to the lack of transparency around pricing, Dacre did not provide any of the medical records from our dog's passport. Dacre has recently told our kennel that they do not have any medical records prior to our dog registering, this demonstrates that they did not record these.

This has caused a significant issue for us. We naively did not keep our dog’s passport as we were led to believe Dacre had recorded this information.

We registered with Dacre as we wanted to support an independent vet. It’s disappointing to have had such a poor experience.

I brought a car back in November 2025, whilst the experience of buying the car was very pleasant and Krystal was very helpful.

Thereafter, has been appalling with the after sales support. First issue was resolved but not through lack of constant chasing, and now a continuing issue with water ingress on the headlight, which I was told was just condensation where the vehicle was sat for some time. Everytime myself or partner call an manager isn't in. I have only once had a returned call, in which I was fobbed off.

Long review and story I'm afraid!

Our experience with this company started out great, then rapidly deteriorated.
I bought a car on Easter Monday. They were brilliant with their information, discussion, and willingness to help throughout the buying process. When I bought the car, I was made aware the battery might be failing, and if this was the case, I could let them know and they would happily replace it. The battery was indeed failing, and they replaced it and fitted it for me within a week.

The other issue I discovered on the day I brought the car home, was that the passenger headlight was broken. This only came up as a fault on the dashboard once I got home. With this being a MOT fail as well as an unidentified problem at the point of sale, I let them know straight away and they said they would be happy for me to book in the job with a garage of my choice, and they would liaise with them in regards to replacing the light. I did exactly this and booked in the job with my local garage and asked them to liaise with JW Autos; passing over all contact information. This is where a series of problems began.

The communication from JW Autos became non-existent. Whenever I called, nobody was available to talk to me. Messages and emails were ignored. I even called at 9am on a Tuesday morning to be told 'everyone is with a customer'...

The date that the work was due to take place was approaching. I eventually got through to someone who advised me they actually wanted to source the part and arrange to get it fitted themselves. So they had completely wasted the time of myself and my local garage. But in any case, I was still grateful they said they would fix it for me.

It was another two weeks of consistently chasing before someone eventually told me the part had been ordered and I was booked in on 30 April for the repair. Leading up to that date - more radio silence. I called on 29 April to ask what the plan was for the following day as I had taken time off work to bring the car in. I was told the part had actually not been ordered and there was 'miscommunication'. I began to voice my frustrations. It didn't seem that difficult of a problem to rectify, yet it was becoming so. So back to persistent chasing for a week to work out if they had ordered and received the part. When they eventually had, they didn't let me know. I called once again and was told 'yes it's here now, we're going to take it personally over to the garage we use - please speak to them now and they will fit it for you tomorrow'. At this point it's gone 6pm in the evening and the garage they'd referred me to were not open...

The next day arrives, I called this other garage to be told they did not have the part and nothing had been brought to them. This was still the case at 3pm. My partner ended up going to the dealership personally to collect it as we had just had enough by this point. I'd also like to add the headlight they had sourced was clearly second-hand and absolutely filthy. He brought it to their recommended garage (who were apparently expecting us) only to be told they had no space or time that day to do the job anyway. We took the part away with us and ended up getting it fitted ourselves. This entire saga which I thought would be a quick fix took nearly 6 weeks to rectify, and it wasn't actually even fully rectified as we ended up completing the work ourselves.

I couldn't recommend this dealership any less, based purely off their after-sales and customer service, or lack there-of. Our entire experience started off so positive, but now I would actively encourage anyone looking to buy or sell a car to avoid this dealership. I was lucky that in the grand scheme of things, my issue was just a headlight. But I now know of other people that have had major mechanical problems with cars they have purchased here and their problems were never resolved and they've subsequently lost large sums of money.

So all in all, the whole experience just feels like a real shame.

The E-Seva portal for booking appointments for miscellaneous consular services is extremely difficult to use and places unnecessary burdens on Indian citizens residing in the UK.
One major issue is the requirement to upload a PDF copy of a Power of Attorney with a passport-sized photo under a strict 200KB file size limit. Previously, this limit was 300KB, and despite this concern being raised earlier, the limit has been reduced rather than increased. Compressing a document like a Power of Attorney—while maintaining legibility and including images—within 200KB is highly impractical.
Additionally, the list of mandatory supporting documents appears excessive and, in some cases, irrelevant. For instance, requiring a copy of a court case or FIR for a Power of Attorney application is unclear and seems unnecessary as in  most applications a court case or FIR is not applicable. We simply want a POA to be attested, that it! These requirements create confusion and delay, especially when applications cannot proceed without uploading documents that may not apply.
The overall process causes significant frustration and stress for applicants who are already navigating complex documentation and attestation procedures.
I strongly urge you to review both the technical constraints (such as file size limits) and the document requirements on the portal. Making these more practical and relevant would greatly improve the user experience for overseas applicants.
An urgent update to the e-Seva portal is needed to address these issues.

I visited The Pilot in February 2026 with my family, including my three elderly grandparents. While the rest of the table ordered fish and chips, I opted for the fish cakes. During the meal, I gave my partner just one single spoonful of my fish cake, and I finished the rest of the plate.
That turned out to be a massive mistake.
A few hours later, I became violently unwell, suffering from severe vomiting and passing blood. The symptoms were so extreme that I had to be admitted to the hospital. My partner was also admitted with milder—but still significant—symptoms. The single spoonful of fish cake was the **only** food we had shared in the last 48 hours. Tellingly, no one else at our table who ate the fish and chips got sick; the illness was entirely isolated to the two of us who consumed the fish cakes.
The physical aftermath has been exhausting. I required heavy medication and had to undergo several medical tests for weeks following the incident just to recover.
What makes this horrific experience even worse was the restaurant's reaction. When we contacted The Pilot to explain what had happened, we weren’t looking for a handout—we called purely as a courtesy to warn them so they could check their kitchen and fish cakes to prevent other customers from getting dangerously ill. Instead, we were met with disdain. Management refused to take any accountability whatsoever, showed zero empathy, and took no action to ensure their customers' safety.
Getting severe food poisoning and being hospitalised as a consequence is awful, but being treated with contempt by the establishment that caused it is extremely concerning.

Attended the Bottomless Brunch on 23rd May and, unfortunately, there were quite a few issues from the very beginning.

When booking, we found out you could only add guests in twos, not individually. I contacted both The Cuban and the agency several times for help and received no reply from either. In the end, I had to ring The Cuban directly just to get one extra person added to the booking.

We were told to arrive promptly for 12:30pm, yet the doors didn’t open until well after that time. There were 22 of us in total, and we were finally seated around 12:50pm, despite drinks supposedly starting from 1pm. Even then, 45 minutes later we still hadn’t received any drinks, while other tables around us had already been served. I personally ordered non-alcoholic drinks and waited 50 minutes for my very first drink to arrive. Our group repeatedly had to ask staff for drinks, only to be told “they’re being made.”

Two members of our party are disabled and both carry disabled ID cards, Blue Badges, and receive PIP. When they asked for the disabled toilet key, staff responded with “well, you’re not disabled.” This was completely unacceptable and deeply inappropriate. Nobody should be questioned like that when asking to use an accessible toilet. To make matters worse, the disabled toilet in the main area was absolutely filthy.

The actual agency running the event itself was exceptional, but sadly the staff at The Cuban really let the experience down. The event was advertised as a “bottomless brunch,” yet the food consisted of just a burger. If you wanted fries, it was an additional £4, and even then the portion was tiny.

It was also an extremely hot day, around 28–29 degrees. Some members of our group smoke, but it was far too hot to comfortably sit outside, so we ended up standing in a tiny corner near the bins to have cigarettes. It was only afterwards that we realised umbrellas were actually available, but no staff member had bothered to put them up during the brunch itself.

Overall, the staff came across as rude, slow, and lacking any urgency or professionalism. It’s such a shame because The Cuban used to be fantastic years ago, and I used to visit regularly in the evenings. Sadly, this experience felt very penny-pinching and badly managed.

Out of the 22 of us who attended, not one person said they would return. Bad reviews come from bad experiences, and unfortunately this was definitely one of them.

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to make a formal complaint regarding the handling of my immigration case by your firm, in particular by Mr Otabek Golumov.

I believe that my case has not been handled with the level of care, diligence, and professionalism that I was entitled to expect.

In addition to my previous concerns, I would like to raise the following serious issue:

I was not advised or supported in seeking an adjournment of my court hearing, despite there being clear reasons to do so. In particular, there was an issue with an expert report which could have been corrected, and further supporting evidence (including a country report) could have been properly prepared and submitted.

I am concerned that this option may not have been pursued due to the associated cost (approximately £1,000), and that financial considerations may have taken priority over the proper handling of my case.

As a result, my case proceeded without key corrections and supporting evidence, which may have negatively affected the outcome.

Furthermore:

I am a father of minor children, and my entire family’s future depends on this case;

Given the seriousness of the risks we face, I find it unacceptable that my case was not handled with the necessary level of care and strategic preparation;

I also feel that my legal representative did not take an active and engaged role in progressing and defending my case.

Given the gravity of these concerns, I request that you:

Provide a full explanation as to why an adjournment was not sought;

Clarify what advice was given to me regarding correcting the expert report and submitting further evidence;

Confirm whether my case was handled in accordance with your professional obligations and standards;

Explain what steps, if any, can now be taken to address the consequences of these decisions.

I request that this complaint be handled in accordance with your formal complaints procedure. I disagree with the firm’s response.

Instead of addressing the issues raised, the firm has chosen to deny that my case relates to them. I find this concerning.

I was a client of the firm and I have documentation to confirm this, including payment records and correspondence. My review reflects my personal experience with their services in relation to my immigration case.

Due to confidentiality, I understand that the firm may not be able to discuss details publicly. However, stating that my experience is “inaccurate” without proper explanation does not address the substance of my concerns.

I remain willing to provide evidence to Trustpilot or any relevant authority if required.

I stand by my review Muraz

I look forward to your response.

I had a very disappointing experience today at Lina Stores Italian Restaurant & Deli Marylebone, and unfortunately it left me feeling uncomfortable and unwelcome.

I visited this morning with a simple plan,  to have a mint tea and possibly order breakfast afterward. I wasn’t in a rush and wanted to take my time to decide. When I arrived, I was greeted by a lady who appears to be assigned to welcome guests at the entrance and seat them at a table. She showed me to my seat and everything started well. I sat down, felt comfortable, and began looking through the menu.

I ordered a mint tea, which was served without any issues. At that point, everything was fine.

However, things quickly changed. The same lady who welcomed and seated me came back to my table and told me that if I was not going to order a breakfast meal, she would need the table at 9am. The way this was communicated made me feel like I was being pushed out, even though I had just arrived and was already a paying customer.

As a customer, I believe I should be allowed to take my time. I had every intention of possibly ordering food, but I didn’t appreciate being rushed or pressured into making a decision. It made me feel like I was obligated to order more just to justify sitting there, which is not how a customer should feel.

The situation became even more uncomfortable. I spoke to another waitress and asked for the name of the lady, but she refused to give it. Then the same lady approached me again and said she did not want to share her name. This made the situation worse and felt unprofessional.

I explained calmly that I was disappointed with how I was being treated. I told her that her behavior and the way she spoke to me were unacceptable. Instead of acknowledging this, she continued to justify herself by saying it gets busy at 9am and that she needed the table because I had not ordered breakfast.

I understand that restaurants get busy, but that does not excuse making a customer feel rushed, uncomfortable, or unwelcome. I repeated that I am still a paying customer and I should be treated with respect, regardless of whether I order food immediately or take my time to decide.

When I asked for the bill so I could pay, the waitress told me that it was “on the house” and that I did not need to pay. Again, I made it clear that I did not want to leave without paying, as I had the money and was willing to pay. My concern was never about the cost, it was about how I was treated. I simply did not want to feel rushed or pushed out while I was still having my tea. I was there as a paying customer and expected to be treated as one. Though I appreciate the gesture of having my bill “on the house”. I hope that the lady should always practice and show kindness to all customers regardless of the situation. Her behaviour is not a good reflection to the restaurant.

Overall, the experience felt awkward, unnecessary, and disappointing. Good customer service is not just about serving food/drinks, it is about how you treat people. Today, I did not feel respected or valued as a customer.

I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves how they communicate with customers in the future. No one should feel pressured or pushed out while simply trying to enjoy a quiet moment with a tea.

rarely leave reviews, but I feel like people need to be warned about my experience with Pinnacle Warranties.

I’ve had two major mechanical failures on my vehicle—a timing chain failure before 60,000 miles and a turbo failure at around 70,000 miles. Both of these are serious issues that you would reasonably expect a warranty to cover.

However, both claims were rejected.

The reason given each time? “Wear and tear.”

This makes absolutely no sense. A timing chain failing before 60,000 miles is not normal wear and tear, and neither is a turbo failing at 70,000 miles—especially when the car has been properly maintained. I’ve already raised these points with them multiple times, but they’ve been completely ignored.
Both garages agreed it is not down to wear and tear the vehicle had full service history and happened due to parts of the car failing (looking into this further they are common faults for this particular model of car and is not down to wear and tear but due to mechanical failure .

What’s most frustrating is that this is exactly why you take out a warranty in the first place—to protect yourself from costly, unexpected mechanical failures. Yet it seems that no matter what it is  they simply refuse to pay out and put everything down to “wear and tear”

In my experience, this warranty has been a complete waste of money. Based on how my claims were handled, it feels like they will find any reason not to cover repairs, no matter how valid the claim is.

I would strongly advise others to think very carefully before purchasing a policy with them.

Not sure if you should avoid Pronovias as a whole brand, or the consultant I had that day, but the experience was very distressing!!!

From the very first dress I tried on, the fitting was extremely uncomfortable. The dresses were tightened to the point where I could barely breathe, and I began to feel dizzy and unwell almost immediately. I mentioned this during the appointment, but it did not seem to be taken seriously. Each time a dress was removed, I felt a huge sense of relief — which should have been a clear sign something was wrong.

The physical handling throughout the appointment was also concerning. My skin was repeatedly caught in the clips while pinning the dresses, which was painful, and even after mentioning it several times, it continued. The same happened when the veil was pinned onto my head — it was very painful, and my discomfort was not properly addressed.

What made the experience worse was the overall atmosphere. I felt rushed throughout, as though the goal was to end the appointment quickly rather than ensure I was comfortable. I was also told that the dress price would increase by 15% if I didn’t decide by the following Monday, which added unnecessary pressure to what should be a special and thoughtful experience.

I left the appointment feeling physically unwell, and even experienced back pain afterwards. Despite liking one of the dresses, the experience itself was so upsetting that I decided not to proceed.

To make matters worse, I sent a detailed follow-up email to the consultant and never received any response, which I find completely unacceptable given the seriousness of what happened.

My friends are now avoiding the place, and I would recommend you do too. This is not the experience you want when looking for the perfect dress.

I had such high expectations for Pronovias, but the experience honestly felt disappointing.

From the moment we arrived, the atmosphere felt rushed rather than special. Appointments like this are meant to be memorable, but we were made to feel like we needed to hurry through everything instead of enjoying the process.

What stood out (in a bad way) was the service — it came across quite cold and dismissive at times. Even small touches, like offering a glass of champagne , felt begrudging rather than welcoming, which added to the overall feeling that we weren’t really valued as customers.

For a brand positioned as premium, I expected a much warmer, more attentive experience. Unfortunately, it felt transactional and slightly uncomfortable instead.

To make matters worse, they kept pestering me to come back afterwards — absolutely not. There was also constant talk about the store closing while multiple customers were still there, which made the whole experience feel even more rushed and uncomfortable.

Overall, it was an awful experience when it should have been a special one.

When I pointed it out they lied and said it was 10mm and the invoice was wrong. Now, because the slab was very hard to level, I had to grind it down, and its obvious that is 20mm aggregate. Due to the aggregate being larger, when I done the pour I had a hard time leveling it correctly and now I have  to spend extra time and money to grind the concrete down. Also I had to pay for extra material (1 cubic meter) as it was more material going in due to it being hard to maneuver and level. Needles to say, I won't be using them again!
But I am concerned about the strength of my slab due to the 110mm thickness with 20mm aggregate.

Following the response from the owner, I have to reiterate the fact that I did complain to IMix at the time, email and phones but they simply didn't admit any wrong doing. They eventually provided cube tests which I didn't witnessed being done when the slab was poured. If the cubes were poured with my material, they would have seen the larger aggregates. Its just the whole behaviour being very shady and not trustworthy. I am downgrading to 1 star because of this.

There were also aspects of the property that we later discovered were apparently “within specification,” despite never being properly explained or highlighted during the sales process. One major example being the significant incline and drainage behaviour within the gardens, which has now become a serious concern.

The current condition of the gardens across multiple neighbouring plots is extremely worrying. We are now experiencing substantial cracking, separation and deep holes forming within the ground only months after completion. Combined with ongoing flooding and drainage concerns, confidence in the underlying ground preparation and external works has significantly reduced.

We are also still dealing with ongoing unresolved issues internally, including a washing machine issue first raised in December which remains unresolved despite multiple visits, videos and repeated communication.

There have also been numerous smaller but frustrating experiences along the way — contractors entering and digging up front gardens without proper notice, parking issues across the development, delays on agreed works, and constant promises of “7–14 days” which regularly turn into months.

Overall, whilst the homes initially appeared promising, the lack of aftercare, poor communication, repeated delays and ongoing unresolved issues have made this an extremely disappointing experience.

The biggest regret of my life was putting my faith in Trio Clinic.

My arms have been left badly mutilated, and I am devastated. I am going through hell. I paid thousands, only to look far worse than I did beforehand. I made it clear that I only wanted skin tightening, but instead I have been left with severe fibrosis and sagging, crepey skin.

At no point, either before or after the operation, was fibrosis ever mentioned to me by the Trio team. I only discovered this once I was back in the UK. Despite the fact that the doctor caused a haematoma, I was never warned that this could lead to fibrosis. Instead, I was repeatedly told that “it’s normal” and that “everything is normal.”

To make matters worse, the clinic says it no longer has the pre-operative photographs taken of my arms the day before surgery. They qshould have retained these records, and I find it extremely suspicious that they now claim to have no record of photographs taken by the Trio Clinic team at the clinic. The photos were taken using proper lighting and a professional camera, and I was asked to turn at every angle. They are now claiming this did not happen. Fortunately, I have evidence to the contrary, but this speaks volumes about the character of the business.

When I asserted my legal data rights and asked for those photos, the manager — who is also the surgeon’s wife — completely changed her attitude towards me. She sent me a threatening message containing false accusations that I had been abusive, along with legal threats if I chose to make my experience public.

Once I was back in the UK, I was told the operation had been successful and that the outcome was now my responsibility. In my experience, the clinic’s promise of lifetime aftercare and guidance, as stated on its website, has proven to be baseless.

When it became clear that the procedure had been complicated and that the results were not as expected, I was treated with coldness and a shocking lack of empathy. I trusted these people with my wellbeing, and their response has been heartbreaking.

The consent form also states: “The one-piece corset/medical bra to be used in the 1st stage after the operation is included in the price [depends on the surgery].”

However, I was not given a medical-grade compression garment. Instead, I was given a poor-quality, badly fitting, locally made garment in Istanbul. Its labels stated that it was not intended for medical, therapeutic, or continual use, and instead described it as shapewear to be worn under clothing.

Proper, even compression immediately after surgery is essential in helping to prevent complications such as seromas. In my case, I was given a strappy corset that did not even cover all of the areas where liposuction had been performed. It dug into my skin, left deep imprints, and rubbed against my incisions, potentially increasing the risk of infection.

At the moment, I am too unwell to go into full detail about everything I experienced and found to be horrendous and unprofessional. But not everything is as it seems. For example, the website claims that patients will stay in a 5-star hotel, yet I was placed in the Hampton by Hilton, which is a 3-star hotel. The discrepancies between what is promised and what is actually delivered go on and on.

I felt that I was not seen as a human being, but simply as a source of income, regardless of whether I was an appropriate candidate for the procedure.

Furthermore, I continue to ask them for my insurance details, which they do not answer. I am now seeking legal representation to handle this matter on my behalf.

If this has happened to you too, I advise you get in touch with the Ministry of Health International Patient Channel. You can call or email. The Turkish Government are trying to prevent unethical medical tourism and will assist you.

Based on my experience, I would strongly advise others not to use this clinic.

He plugged his scanner into my ODB2 Port, and he informed me that the computer would not communicate with my car. So he proceeded to try another scanning tool, and the same outcome, it would not communicate with my car. So while he was there, I did a Google search, and found a forum relating to his scanning tool, which suggested that the firmware should probably be updated in relation to my car, a Mazda. The Snapon scanner connected straight away, and he was able to diagnose the fault which turned out to be a faulty exhaust pressure sensor, which he was able to replace for just the cost of the part, as he ordered one from his supplier before finishing work, on the off chance that this would be the problem. We then sprayed DPF cleaner into the DPF, and forced a Regen, and so far so good, the fault code is gone, and my peace of mind has been restored.

I recently cancelled my membership after a very disappointing experience, both in terms of customer service and overall value for money.

During my fixed-term contract, my monthly fee was increased from £144 to £160 without any improvements to the facilities or services. When I challenged this, rather than addressing the concern or offering a fair resolution, I was effectively invited to cancel my membership.

* The studios are very small, which impacts the quality of classes
* The class booking system is poorly managed—popular classes appear full, yet attendance often doesn’t reflect this, and there is no real incentive for members to cancel unused bookings

Within those 6 months, we were covered by the warranty, meaning Grant had to legally pay for the issues as they were issues that came with the car upon purchase and for those issues under the Consumer Rights Act 2015. He sold us a faulty car and claimed that it had been checked over before the sale.

We went to different and independent mechanics, and they all said that the car had barely received an inspection before sale, it was just enough to pass the MOT. When contacting Grant, not only did he tells us we had to pay to fix those things out of our own pockets as he has a small business and cannot afford to pay for these things (even though the warranty and the law says he must do so), he is currently trying to force us to pay him back for 1/3 of the problems he helped to pay for. And the cherry on top: he is threatening to take US TO COURT for something that could have been avoided if he had carried out an adequate inspection of the car.

We were met with: A flat battery which had to get completely replaced, 4 worn out break pads which were a safety issue and had to get replaced, and just last week, we had a loose piece at the front of the car; the crank pulley was loose, very worn out, and making noises when driving. The total of all of this was a whooping cost of £900, £400 of which we paid, £500 of which he is asking us to pay half of, as if he wasn't legally required to pay the £500 anyway.

Grant doesn't operate on a good faith basis, he wants to sell you a car full of problems and blame it on you when you try to take it up with him. He is nice and kind at the beginning to make you feel bad for trying to make him pay for the car, with the excuse that he is a "small business", even though he is legally required to pay. I really hate leaving negative reviews, and avoid them when I can, but when it comes to something as serious and as expensive as a car, this is no longer a joking matter. And I see I am not alone in this given I have seen plently of reviews pointing to the same issue.

Avoid this dealership if you can, and hold Grant to account where he is trying to avoid liability for the faulty products he is selling.

one_star_reviews.text: No "passion" for retro at all. At my workplace i got a A500 board in that had been recapped by them. They used way too tall capacitors, (so a CDTV-RAM-IDE wouldnt fit) and the soldering wasnt done through and through, very very sloppy and only at the bottom of the PCB. 2 capacitors had a loose leg, and the soldering looked like it was done in a rush or with a heavily underpowered soldering iron, the solder was not flowed into place but just a big blob barely making any contact. This is NOT how you "fix" priceless retro computers.

I sent a rare prototype Amiga 3500 motherboard (the blue one) for a battery repair in March, along with two CD32 boards, an FMV module, and a CS MkII. I did not get them back until December — nine months, with nearly no communication. I had to send a physical letter to get any response at all. When the parcel finally arrived, it had been addressed to my online nickname rather than my legal name, so it was refused by customs and returned to the UK. I had to pay shipping again, plus Brexit import taxes running into several hundreds of euros — for a mistake that was entirely his. The packing was a single cardboard box with the CD32 boards placed directly on top of the 3500 motherboard, scratching the surface. The recapping work itself left solder balls and bridges across multiple tracks. The FPU was dead on arrival. The Zorro 3 slots no longer worked. The board ran hot. The FMV metal shield was physically torn. The replacement capacitors were oversized, causing the shield to protrude. The CD32 boards are correctly recapped — SMD work is fine. But through-hole work is clearly not within his competence, and a prototype of this rarity should never have been touched without that competence. A second professional had to document the full extent of the damage. Total loss: over €1,000, not counting the damage to the board itself. One year of stress. No acknowledgement of any error — not the addressing, not the packing, not the workmanship. I will not be using UK repairers again for this reason. My boards now go to Scandinavia.

I have friends who bring their dogs to this pub with no problems. Obviously this scenario will all be recorded on the bar camera.
Under the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991, it is a criminal offence to allow any dog to be "dangerously out of control" in public or private, defined as injuring someone or making them fear injury. Penalties include unlimited fines and up to 5 years in prison
Definition of "Dangerous": A dog is considered dangerous if it acts aggressively, bites, or causes someone to fear for their safety. This applies to all breeds.

I see this as more of a responsible review for public safety as opposed to a review slagging of the whole Pub.
As I believe this is a dangerous dog and shouldn’t be in a public bar. Which is the responsibility partly of the owner and of the pub manager/premises license holder..

ARK said somebody would be in touch in 48 hours to arrange a visit. 72 hours later nobody contact me. So I called them, they said somebody would be in touch shortly.

I then got a text saying somebody would be coming on the 8th May. No time, nothing. So again I called. They said they would be there at 8am but that I should also note that they have all day appointments. I said I wouldn't be there at that time they said they would call back that same day before 5pm with an alternative time.

Guess what. They didn't call me back.

So I called and they were not even aware that I had called previously. They instead apologised that they had not been on time, the technician was ill so the replacement would be there in the next hour so between 11:30am-12:30am. I had to explain again that they had not confirmed a time and I was not at the property to which the lady said, well then we will have to rebook you and it could take up to 2 weeks because there is only 1 technician in my area.

I'm convinced my housing association doesn’t know about the long wait times which actually make the problem worse. Call me cynical but perhaps this is their aim. A worse infestation means longer treatment. They simply do not care and do not have the required amount of technicians to effectively solve any pest problems. Choose a different company.

I would expect the company to ensure that all drivers maintain appropriate road safety standards, particularly when operating branded vehicles in public traffic.

Very disappointing experience at Fitzrovia Pharmacy on Great Portland Street.I went there with a private prescription for my child and was charged £106.38 for Azithromycin suspension and soluble Prednisolone tablets. I appreciate private prescriptions can be expensive, but I was surprised that the price wasn’t mentioned before the medicines were prepared.I was only told the total at the counter, just before paying, after everything had already been dispensed. When I questioned it, I was told it made no difference whether the price was given before or after dispensing, as long as it was before payment. I don’t agree with that. With a private prescription, I believe the cost should be made clear upfront, so patients can make an informed choice and have the option to take the prescription elsewhere.Overall, I found the whole experience disappointing and I wouldn’t use this pharmacy again for a private prescription.

Beware of Crystal Travel’s "deals." They use high-pressure sales calls and fake British names to push tickets that are often more expensive than the airline’s own app. They will claim that "UK Government Taxes" are non-refundable to pocket your money. Under UK law, Air Passenger Duty (APD) MUST be refunded if the flight is not taken.

If they refuse your refund, demand a full breakdown of the taxes, quote the Consumer Rights Act 2015, and lodge a formal complaint with the airline directly to get a reference number. Don't be rushed into closing a deal; they only fold when you cite the law and follow up persistently. It took 5 weeks, but I got my full refund. Save yourself the stress and book directly with the airline.

Unfortunately, I would not recommend Andrew Lutterlock from Kenneth Elliot & Rowe, especially for first-time buyers who might need guidance and communication throughout the process.

While he was one of the more expensive quotes we received, the service didn’t reflected that. Communication was extremely poor from start to finish. Emails regularly went unanswered, and the only reliable way to contact him was by phone. Even then, it often felt as though he was scrambling to locate our file and had very little understanding of what stage our purchase was at.

We were asked multiple times whether we had received our mortgage offer, despite both myself and our broker sending this to Andrew over three months earlier. At one stage, when we visited the Romford office to have documents witnessed in person to speed up exchange, he again asked whether we had our mortgage offer — despite us being due to exchange within 48 hours.

During this meeting with Andrew I also noticed paperwork incorrectly marked us as first-time buyers, even though I was simultaneously selling another property.(Andrew wasn’t doing my sale process) I quickly made Andrew aware of this before signing.
Having sold several properties previously, I understood the conveyancing process well enough to recognise this was a significant oversight. It raised concerns about how little attention had been paid to our file, particularly regarding the source of deposit funds and basic case details.

Approaching completion, communication became even worse. We were unable to get hold of Andrew by phone or email while trying to confirm whether funds had been received in form of our deposit & if our mortgage had been cleared for completion the following day. Eventually, the accounts department — who were excellent — investigated for us and confirmed everything was received & ready. We then discovered Andrew was off sick & would likely be for the week, there had been no handover to another solicitor and no communication to us that someone else would be handling our cas.

On completion day itself, we called around 1pm and again around 3–4pm for updates, with no information provided. We finally received confirmation of completion at around 6pm. Thankfully, the sellers had exchanged numbers with us directly beforehand because without that communication, I genuinely believe the move could have fallen through.

To make matters worse, 6–8 weeks after completion and settling into our new home, Andrew emailed to say he had made an error on our final bill and requested additional payment to correct his own mistake. Although the amount was not huge, I did not feel this was our responsibility. After questioning it, he eventually agreed it would be covered.

Unfortunately, you do not truly know how good a solicitor is until you are deep into the process and it is too late to change.

That is exactly why I felt it was important to leave this review for others considering using him.We can’t speak on behalf of the whole team as this would be unfair judgement however we can firmly say we wouldn’t recommend Andrew Lutterlock for any conveyance matters.

I have had the worst experience ever with this company. I would never recommend them to anyone again.

Around 10 years ago, I used this firm for another legal process with a lawyer called Thiago, who was extremely competent. Because of that positive experience, when I needed legal assistance again years later, they were the first company that came to mind.

I started a process with Isabella in February 2025 regarding wedding paperwork that needed to be completed before my wedding at the end of August. I was originally told that the entire process would take approximately four months and should have been finalised by June 2025 at the latest.

However, the process ended up taking over one year to be completed.

By June nothing was ready, and the same happened in July. The amount of stress that my partner and I went through was completely unnecessary, especially during what should have been a very happy period of our lives.

In the end, we had to get married without the proper ceremony because the documents were never completed on time.

After that, I spent months chasing updates through emails, phone calls, and WhatsApp messages, but Isabella — the lawyer I had signed the contract with — simply disappeared. She stopped replying to emails, messages, and calls.

When she finally decided to respond, she claimed that Brazilian law had changed and that the process would take longer. However, she never provided any proof, documentation, emails, or official evidence to support this explanation — only words.

October, November, and December passed with absolutely no updates from either Isabella or the company.

By January 2026, almost one year after starting the process, my partner and I decided to escalate the matter to HR because we genuinely felt we had been scammed and that the company had disappeared with our money. I had paid £4,000 upfront.

We then contacted the general email address listed on their website. A few days later, Martha from HR replied and said we would receive a solution within 14 days.

February 2026 marked exactly one year since the process had started, and after those 14 days passed, once again I heard nothing from anyone.

Eventually, I was passed to another lawyer whose name I cannot even remember.

By that point, my stress levels were beyond extreme. I felt exhausted, disappointed, angry, and genuinely shocked that this situation was still continuing after so long.

They asked me to come into the office for a meeting, but I refused because I did not want to go through the entire story again, especially considering how frustrated I already was.

Then, completely out of nowhere, one day I simply received all my documents at home — with no email, no explanation, no apology, and no communication whatsoever.

Conclusion: this company does not care about you, your process, your deadlines, or your personal life. The office is full of incompetent people who do not understand what proper client care means.

If you are thinking about starting a process with this company, please think twice — or even four times. I am sure there are far more professional and reputable firms out there.

I would never recommend this company or this experience to anyone ever again.

This shopping centre charges £1 for toilet access, which is something virtually every other mall includes as part of the cost of doing business and built into the rent/service charges for tenants. I genuinely do not understand why this place feels the need to make itself “special” over basic toilet access.

I had my young son with me in a buggy and wanted to use the toilet, but the security guard told me the baby facilities were only in the ladies’ toilets, so I had to wait for my wife to arrive. While waiting, I witnessed another customer arguing with the guard for around 10 minutes regarding the £1 refund policy.

The customer had spent 88p in one of the shops, but the guard refused to refund the £1, claiming there was a minimum spend requirement. The problem is the sign directly in front of him clearly stated that customers simply needed to show proof of purchase. It did not mention any minimum spend whatsoever. The guard either could not understand the English on the sign or was simply making up rules as he went along.

A lawyer who happened to overhear the argument intervened and spoke directly to the owners, explaining that the signage was clear and they could not invent extra conditions that were not written there. Only after that discussion did one of the owners instruct the guard to refund the customer.

Around 15 minutes later my wife arrived, having already spent around £30 downstairs. I told her to go in first with our son because by this point I had zero confidence the guard would apply any common sense. After she came back out, I went to use the toilet and the same guard again demanded proof of purchase from me personally, despite the fact he had already made me wait specifically because I was with a child needing the baby facilities.

Inside, the facilities were poor anyway: no toilet seat, no tissue paper, and a wet floor. Absolutely nothing about the toilets justified charging people separately to use them.

On the way out I spoke to both owners and pointed out that their own sign says “parents” can use the baby facilities, which clearly implies both parents, not just one. The owner agreed with me. I also told them they seriously need to train their staff properly because the communication and understanding from the guard was unacceptable.

Overall, the entire experience felt unnecessarily hostile, embarrassing, and badly managed over £1. There are plenty of other places on Green Street with similar shops and food options that do not create this kind of hassle for customers.

I would like to make a formal complaint regarding the unacceptable treatment and conditions at the public toilets.

The security guard on duty requires proper training regarding hidden disabilities and the legal rights of disabled people in the UK. A person using a disabled toilet with a National Disability Card and RADAR key should not be spoken to disrespectfully, challenged inappropriately, or subjected to abuse of authority. Hidden disabilities are protected under the Equality Act 2010, and staff must not discriminate against disabled individuals.

The Equality Act 2010 requires service providers to make reasonable adjustments for disabled people, including access to accessible toilets. A RADAR key system is designed specifically to allow disabled users access to facilities safely and with dignity. Staff do not have the authority to ignore or override disability rights simply because of notices written on a whiteboard or their own personal opinions.

This matter should be investigated by the local council and Trading Standards, especially if members of the public are being charged to use facilities that are poorly maintained, unhygienic, and potentially in breach of public health standards.

The female toilets smell strongly due to bins not being emptied regularly, and the toilets themselves are not maintained to an acceptable standard. This is completely unacceptable, especially when people are paying by cash or card to use these facilities. Hygiene, cleanliness, and maintenance standards must be upheld.

This is the United Kingdom, where disability rights, public hygiene regulations, and consumer protection laws must be followed properly. The current condition of these toilets and the behaviour of staff are disgraceful and require urgent attention. I did not provide consent for Starling Bank to conduct internet surveillance on my business website, nor did I consent to the harvesting, scraping, or logging of my health profile. I had a distressing experience last week that I feel compelled to share. Immediately after picking up my dog from Hersden Dog Spa, I noticed she was in visible discomfort. By the time we arrived home, her condition had deteriorated so rapidly that I rushed her to the emergency vet. She was diagnosed with ulcers in both eyes, which the vet confirmed were directly related to the grooming session—likely due to shampoo irritation or improper hairdryer use.
​My dog spent three days unable to open her eyes and has required three different medications for over a week. While the groomer initially offered to cover the first vet bill, their subsequent response has been deeply unprofessional. They dismissed the injury as "very superficial" and claimed the grooming was "satisfactory," refusing to refund the groom or cover the additional vet fees required for her recovery.
​It is highly unprofessional to label a session "satisfactory" when it results in a serious medical injury. Furthermore, the actual quality of the groom was very poor; she had uneven patches of hair left all over her face and eyes, looking as though it had been haphazardly chopped here and there.
​Taking full responsibility for a pet’s safety and providing a quality service are fundamental parts of being a professional groomer. Unfortunately, that was not my experience here, and I cannot recommend this establishment.

I have attached photos of the snap and the right side corrosion to the rear subframe.

🔧 Dealer’s responsibility (first 6 months)
1. Faults are assumed to be there at sale
If something goes wrong within 6 months:
It is legally presumed the fault existed when you bought the car
The dealer has to prove it didn’t, not the other way around
2. The car must meet 3 standards
The vehicle must be:
Of satisfactory quality (safe, durable, no major hidden issues)
Fit for purpose (drives properly, roadworthy)
As described (matches advert/spec)
A snapped subframe, major corrosion, engine failure etc. would clearly fail this.
3. Dealer must fix it (or refund)
If a fault appears:
You must give the dealer one chance to repair or replace
The repair must be:
Free of charge
Done within a reasonable time
Without causing major inconvenience
4. If they can’t fix it
If the repair fails, is refused, or takes too long:
You can reject the car and get a refund
OR keep it and ask for a price reduction
⚠️ After 30 days but within 6 months:
The dealer can make a deduction for usage from your refund
5. Costs related to the fault
The dealer is responsible for reasonable costs caused by the issue, which can include:
Recovery/towing (in many cases)
Transport related to getting the car fixed
🚫 What they can’t do
They can’t say “sold as seen” to avoid responsibility
They can’t force you to pay for repairs for a pre-existing fault
They can’t ignore you or delay unreasonably

All in all we absolutely would not return. We have dined here a few times over the years and always had a lovely meal. Today has left a bad taste in our mouth and we would not recommend others come here.

Purchased a white Astra from Kingsway Motors on 01/05/26. Within a week (around 07/05/26), I noticed a scraping noise coming from the rear when driving and braking. I contacted the dealership the next morning and was advised to go through my RAC plan. After waiting for an appointment, a garage inspected the car on 15/05/26 and advised that the brake pads and discs were worn and needed replacing, quoting around £300.

Given I had only just purchased the car, I contacted Kingsway Motors expecting support. Unfortunately, I found the response quite defensive from the outset, with comments such as “this doesn’t happen with our cars” and questioning the repair quote. I was told to bring the car back for inspection, which may sound reasonable, but due to distance and logistics this would have meant additional cost, time off, and being left without a vehicle, especially as no courtesy car was available.

When I explained that, given the circumstances, I was considering returning the car instead, the tone of the conversation changed and I felt the response became defensive. I was told I was “jumping the gun” and reminded that “it’s a used car, sometimes these things happen.” While I appreciate used cars can develop faults, this was less than a week after purchase and involved the brakes, which understandably affected my confidence in the vehicle and the aftercare I received.
I ultimately chose to pay for the repair myself for peace of mind, but I was disappointed both by the issue arising so soon after purchase and by how my concerns were handled.

I don’t leave reviews lightly, but I feel people should know both about my experience with the vehicle and, more importantly, the customer service that followed.

******Following Response******

You claim to carry out checks on vehicles before they are sold, so I would like to know exactly what these checks consist of, because clearly something was missed.

I already explained that the issue was with both the brake discs and brake pads. The mechanic at the garage even offered to speak with you directly regarding the problem, and you chose not to speak with him.

As for why I did not return the car to you for repair, I have already explained this. It made no sense for me to make the journey given the distance involved, especially when you could not provide a replacement vehicle.

On top of that, after the experience I had and reading similar reviews from other customers, I had very little confidence that the issue would be fixed properly. Based on everything since, I believe I made the right decision.

Before buying a car from here, please take a moment to read the 1-star reviews. Many describe similar experiences with vehicle faults and a total lack of after-sale support.

A fault with my partner and I's car was reported on the day of purchase (engine misfire fault). The car was returned to Kingsway multiple times, the issue was repeatedly misdiagnosed and repairs such as coil packs and spark plugs didn't resolve it. The car was then sent by Kingsway to another garage where the same misdiagnosis was made and the fault remained unresolved.

We found Kingsway's communication poor, and while waiting months for further investigation, we were assured the car was safe to drive and to continue using it. But, as the car reached the end of the 6 month Consumer Right's period, Kingsway began to dispute their responsibility.

When asked for a refund of the vehicle (as per our rights, given multiple failures to repair), a significant deduction for mileage was proposed (90% of the car cost). Mileage that accumulated while Kingsway postponed further investigation and struggled to resolve the day one fault. Multiple opportunities were given to fix the issue, but we found the attitude of staff to be dismissive, rude, and highly unprofessional.

We ultimately took the car to Vauxhall directly, who were able to diagnose and repair the fault in a week - Kingsway won't pay for this. Kingsway insisted we wait months for their auto-electrician, but Vauxhall identified it as an issue with the fuel injection system. Within the first 6 months, independent garages also found a faulty thermostat and cracked exhaust pipe which we paid for ourselves.

I would strongly reconsider purchasing from Kingsway. I do not feel confident in their pre-sale checks, after sales handling, nor their resolution measures - not worth the risk.
