13/04/26 - I am extremely disappointed with the handling of my tenancy by this agency.
If a zero-star rating were possible, that would more accurately reflect my experience.
Following repeated reports of serious issues within the property — including damp, mould, heat loss, and inadequate ventilation — I have received no meaningful resolution, no transparency, and no accountability.
A formal damp survey was carried out on 31 March, yet the findings have not been disclosed or made available to me. Instead, communication has been inconsistent, dismissive, and at times contradictory.
On multiple occasions, I have raised concerns regarding blocked ventilation points within a Grade II listed building, possible structural defects, and the resulting impact on indoor air quality. These concerns have not been addressed in any adequate or timely manner since I moved in in December 2025 (evidence reported within the check-in!).
In the meantime, I have experienced respiratory symptoms requiring A&E medical attention, adding a serious dimension to what is already a concerning situation, but of course so far, indeed, they have tried to fault me in any possible way saying "you don't open the window enough"!
Particularly troubling is the apparent lack of understanding of legal responsibilities in relation to tenant protection — especially in cases involving vulnerability. I have a recognised disability, and the way this matter has been handled does not reflect an appropriate standard of care or awareness.
Recent correspondence has referenced a desire to reach an “amicable resolution.” However, this has not been supported by any concrete actions, clear timelines, or acknowledgment of the issues raised.
The matter has now been formally escalated to both the Council and the Conservation Office, and a Council inspection has been carried out. Further updates will follow soon.

Based on my experience, I would strongly advise prospective tenants to proceed with caution, inspect thoroughly the flats when on viewing, and check accordingly the check-in report without delay! It is also noteworthy that while the majority of positive reviews appear focused on property sales, many of the one-star reviews relating to rentals appear to raise recurring concerns connected to damp and mould issues within the rented properties.
Also check reviews on https://www.allagents.co.uk/greenleaf-property.com

Update 10/05/26:  Following a Subject Access Request (SAR - GDPR UK), I finally obtained a copy of the damp survey carried out on 31 March 2026.
The report explicitly confirms the presence of mould in both the bathroom and kitchen, alongside external structural contributing defects like cracks on the walls, and ventilation issues described as 'not compliant with Building Regulations'. The damp survey also recommends specialist mould remediation treatment and ventilation improvements, which appears entirely inconsistent with the repeated “tenant lifestyle” explanations previously suggested by the agency, including by Amelia and Robin, the agency director.
A formal complaint also remains unresolved. I am currently still awaiting a substantive response from the agency director following referral to an external paralegal, which I understand is expected by 15 May 2026.

Further updates will follow once the Council inspection report and the findings from the Conservation Office become available. Stay tuned!

Last week, I had not one, but two, incredibly unpleasant encounters with two separate staff members at my young sons, and after that I will never set foot into this store ever again.

I didn't bother to question why the rack was still out on the shop floor if there was a clear health and safety issue with it - I just gathered up my children and left the store.

I then decided to give the store another chance the next week when I went in with my 4 year old son. A female member of staff shouted (again at the top of her lungs) 'DON'T TURN THE PAGES LIKE THAT!' when my 4 year old went to turn a page by folding it over. one_star_reviews.text:
DO NOT GO TO THIS SURGEON.

I went in for purely cosmetic reasons, and it has turned into the worst decision of my life. I had double jaw surgery, which had left me with an overly long chin and a face that looked disproportionate, bulky, and masculine. Instead of any improvement, I’ve been left far worse than I ever was to begin with.

Since the surgery, I’ve been left dealing with constant and serious issues: ongoing mucus drip, breathing problems, a severely deviated septum, a severe perforation (large hole in nose), tonsil stones, recurring sores in my nose, ear pain, and a constant tight, painful sensation in my face and gums, like something is being screwed tighter and tighter. I now get sick all the time, and feel more exhausted than I ever have in my life.

after surgery  I was told there was “nothing wrong” with my face, yet other surgeons have since said otherwise. I feel completely misled and not properly informed about the risks or possible outcomes. This has had a huge impact on my daily life and overall health.

I’ve already had to undergo further surgery elsewhere to try and fix both cosmetic and functional damage and I still need more.

Not only has this affected my health and appearance, but it has also had a serious financial impact. I am now in severe debt as a result of this surgery and the corrective procedures I’ve had to seek elsewhere. Despite everything, the only support I was offered was a referral to the NHS, with no real accountability or help beyond that.

I trusted this surgeon, and that trust was completely misplaced. I was not given the full picture, and I am now living with the consequences every single day.

To make things worse, I was told that I didn’t even need double jaw surgery in the first place. That alone is extremely concerning, especially considering everything I’ve been put through since.

Avoid at all costs.

We signed up for this surgery based on the seemingly positive Google reviews and it was a huge mistake.

Scheduling our first appointment was a nightmare when the incredibly rude receptionist refused to book the routine 6-week check for our newborn with a GP and said we’d have to wait until 8-weeks and get it done simultaneously with her vaccinations with a nurse. My own 6-week check would be delayed as well. This was solely so they would have fewer appointments to manage not because it is recommended by the NHS or safe. We explained we wanted to follow the standard routine as we did with our 2-year old. She eventually said she agreed, only to book the 8-week appointments as she preferred. Three painful phone calls later a nurse finally called and the appointments were arranged per the standard 6-week NHS schedule.

Cutting corners for newborns and mothers is disgraceful.

The day of the appointment comes. We WAITED OVER 90 MINUTES in the waiting room for our scheduled appointment. Eventually there were five prams and sets of angry parents so the GPs finally started divvying up the patients. When we were eventually seen, the GP was incredibly distracted. Four different individuals interrupted the appointment and I had to remind her twice that I needed to be physically checked as well having just given birth.

They moved our newborn to the Nursing room for her check and it was no better there in terms of privacy or being interrupted. So much so we left uncomfortable with the quality of her check and had to ask for it to be re-done before her 8-week check. The GP agreed, and then booked the appointment for the wrong time, so i had to call yet again to fix it after receiving incorrect reminder text messages.

The final straw was receiving a phone call an hour before our daughter’s 12-week vaccinations that they’d been cancelled and they’d call next week to arrange another time. Apparently one nurse was on holiday and the other had been off sick and no provisions were made for a locum. We were due to be travelling right after her 16-week vaccinations to see family so we wanted to maintain her schedule.

Additionally, given the current measles outbreak in North London and how often we’re told how important the vaccines are, how flippant the surgery was about cancelling them with no plan was shocking. We actually found another practice willing to do them locally and told the GP surgery which one, but the GP refused to refer us. This happened once with our previous practice when we lived in another borough (cancelled vaccine) and the surgery called us with a plan to visit another surgery so it is possible to maintain the schedule. We were assured we’d be contacted with a solution within a day, five days later we received a phone call to call reception to reschedule but we had already applied to move surgeries.

I am extremely disappointed with my experience with VitalityHealth.

I requested authorisation for treatment for Thyroid Eye Disease in early February 2026. Despite having a Vitality GP referral and seeing their recommended ophthalmologist, they asked me to get my own NHS GP form, which I submitted three times, including specialist reports and GP forms. However, my claim remains pending for several weeks (12 weeks) with no clear decision, timeframe, or treatment pathway.

My condition was diagnosed as active, where early treatment is critical to prevent irreversible changes, including optic nerve compression and potential vision loss. Due to the delay and lack of authorisation, I was left with no option but to self-fund part of my treatment privately and continue care via the NHS.

In contrast, the care I received from Moorfields Eye Hospital (NHS) was prompt and excellent. I have since been referred to St Bartholomew’s Hospital (NHS) for radiotherapy as second-line treatment, again with minimal waiting time and an excellent clinical team.

Meanwhile, my private insurer has still not reached a decision, and the non-clinical customer service teams have been unable to coordinate effectively or involve an appropriate clinical review despite the urgency of the situation.

There appeared to be poor coordination between departments, repeated requests for information already provided, and a lack of clear accountability. Even after raising a formal complaint, responses have been slow and have not addressed the core issue of delayed clinical decision-making.

For a private health insurer, I expected a far more efficient and clinically responsive service—particularly for a time-sensitive condition.

I hope Vitality reviews its processes to ensure patients are not left without timely access to care.

Reply to Vitality Owner' response
Thank you for your response.
I have already contacted Vitality multiple times via phone, email and formal complaint channels over several weeks without resolution.
My concern has not been lack of contact, but the prolonged delay in authorisation and absence of a clear clinical decision or treatment pathway.
Given the nature of my condition and the urgency involved, I would expect this to be addressed through appropriate internal escalation rather than being redirected back to general customer service channels.
I would appreciate this being reviewed by the relevant clinical and authorisation teams, and for a clear written update to be provided to me as a priority.

I engaged Va Va Voom Videos in early 2025 for video editing services. The first six months were positive and I had no issues with the work delivered.

In mid-2025 my business direction changed and I asked to amend my package. A new 12-month arrangement was agreed by email. From the start of 2026 onwards, in my experience the service fell short of what I needed. I found deliveries were frequently late, and I felt the videos did not reflect the LinkedIn corporate style I had briefed, despite my providing overlay text to simplify the process.

I paid my February and March invoices in full as the work had been carried out. After a third month of issues, I requested to end the arrangement on the basis that, in my view, the service I was receiving was not usable for my business. A cancellation fee was applied, plus additional monthly charges while the settlement remained unpaid.

I took legal advice and was advised that the contract terms required me to pay. I accept that outcome, but as a small business owner I wanted to share my honest experience: ending the arrangement has cost me a considerable sum of money, despite my view that the work in the final months was delivered late and was not in a form I could use. Other small businesses may want to scrutinise the cancellation terms carefully before signing.

This review reflects my personal experience.

This was the worst company I dealt with while getting solar and battery quotes.

The sales representative arrived around 20-30 minutes late, which was not a great start.

He then presented the system and, from my perspective, went over the top in claiming it was far superior to other companies. There was a strong emphasis on the panels being Spanish and the battery being Duracell, alongside suggestions that other installers used Chinese equipment which should be avoided.

From that point on, the sales approach felt overly forceful. I was told their price was only available if I signed up that same day, as they were “working nearby”, and that I would not be given time to consider other quotes.

I made it clear that we were still speaking to other companies and that I would provide a decision within a few days. This was repeatedly pushed back on. Instead, I was asked which companies I had contacted and then given negative comments about each of them.

I also felt I was being led into agreeing with a series of questions, such as whether I wanted him to act as my project manager and whether I wanted to reduce my energy bills, which added to the pressure.

I explained that I needed to speak with my father, who is a joint homeowner. This was dismissed, with the suggestion that he would simply agree with me anyway.

There was then an attempt to proceed with a finance check, which I stopped as I had not agreed to go ahead and was not comfortable with a hard search at that stage.

I was also told that because I had contacted multiple companies, I would not be given time to decide, and was questioned on why I had obtained several quotes at all.

The representative then pushed to return the next day when my father would be present, stating that any later would not be possible. Later that day I confirmed that we would not be proceeding.

I cannot comment on the quality of the equipment, but based on the sales process I experienced, I would not feel comfortable using this company.

Overall, I found the approach highly pressurised and uncomfortable, and well outside what I would consider a reasonable sales process. I would not recommend.

I’d like to first of all say that my review does not reflect the space itself which is very clean or the people who were mostly respectful and nice BUT I have to stand up for myself as a paying individual against misinformation and misleading people when it comes to health costs. I went to LIPS for an ENT appointment. At the time of the appointment, Dr. Wong offered to perform a small procedure (I believe it was a nasal endoscopy but I’m not sure) which took about 5-10 mins. When I inquired as to the cost (as one does because private medical is very costly), he said somewhere in the £150-200 range and I said OK. At the end of the appointment, we settled the price at £495 at the Lips front desk, the initial consultation fee along with the cost of the additional procedure and I paid this the day of the appointment in July 2025 which I confirmed with the Lips team. Feb 2026 (7 MONTHS LATER) I am receiving notice of another £510 facility fee. I expressed my confusion to both Lips and Dr. Wongs team as this was never disclosed to me as an additional cost at the time of the appointment and I am only now alerted to this cost in writing 7 months after my appointment. Had I been notified of a facility fee in addition to the procedure cost I already paid of £495, I would have never agreed to the procedure or even the appointment. I feel very mislead and upset with the whole situation and will say not be returning to LIPS again as I feel they were not cost transparent at all which is so necessary when so many medical facilities can be so predatory towards scared individuals seeking help and assurance.

I’ve attended two weddings at The Barnyard in Kent over the past 18 months, and unfortunately, both experiences left me feeling compelled to share some honest feedback.

There’s no denying that the setting itself is beautiful. The venue is clearly chosen for its picturesque surroundings, and on the surface, it creates the perfect backdrop for a wedding day. However, beyond the aesthetics, the experience quickly begins to fall short—and quite significantly.

Across both weddings, there were consistent issues that simply can’t be overlooked. The most concerning aspect was the conduct of the staff, particularly those in senior or ownership positions. On both occasions, I witnessed what I can only describe as rude and dismissive behavior toward the couples and their families. This wasn’t an isolated incident or a one-off bad day—it was a pattern.

A wedding day should feel supportive, smooth, and celebratory. Instead, there seemed to be unnecessary tension caused by the very people responsible for hosting the event. It was uncomfortable to watch, especially knowing how much effort and emotion goes into planning such an important day.

Beyond the service, the food and drinks were also disappointing. Expectations are naturally high for weddings, but in both cases, the quality did not meet even a reasonable standard. It felt like another area where the venue failed to deliver on what should be a memorable experience.

What’s particularly striking is that the couples themselves have been hesitant to speak openly about their experiences—understandably so, as no one wants to overshadow their own wedding memories. But that silence can leave future couples unaware of what they might encounter.

In summary, while The Barnyard offers a stunning setting, it is let down by poor service, disappointing catering, and unprofessional behavior from senior staff. For such an important occasion, couples deserve far better. I would strongly encourage anyone considering this venue to look beyond the appearance and carefully weigh the overall experience.

Whenever I email, I’m given very little information and the responses often come across as dismissive or rude. I even received a phone call today that wasn’t even intended for me. The last two times I requested an update, my emails were largely ignored and only one of my questions was answered.

At this point, I feel completely lost and am honestly considering starting the process elsewhere because I no longer believe I’ll ever receive the report. I would genuinely recommend saving yourself the stress and looking elsewhere. I don’t understand how they think treating patients — especially those suspected to be neurodivergent — in this way is acceptable or helpful.

I was referred to RTN through Right to Choose on 29th December 2025. After waiting 19 weeks, I finally received initial contact by email. Around a week later I was sent questionnaires, which I completed and returned within 48 hours.

After doing everything requested promptly, I then received another email stating it would be approximately 8 months before I would even receive an assessment appointment.

I appreciate that ADHD services across the UK are under huge pressure, but what is frustrating is the lack of transparency around realistic waiting times from the beginning. Patients are already struggling significantly by the time they seek help, and many are holding onto hope that Right to Choose providers will offer a more manageable timeline.

It feels misleading to wait nearly 5 months just for first contact, only to then be told there may be another 8 month wait before assessment. For people seeking ADHD support, especially those already struggling with work, mental health, organisation and daily functioning, this level of delay can have a serious impact.

Providers offering ADHD services have a duty of care not only clinically, but also in communicating honestly and transparently about realistic waiting times so patients can make informed decisions about whether to remain in the queue or seek alternative support. I have emailed and called but to no avail, I can’t fault the staff on the phone as I can imagine they have a horrible time trying to fight fires with the misleading time frames but RTN needs to do better!

I paid RTN Mental Health Solutions £1,074 for an assessment in 2025. In December 2025, the company informed me they were unable to help and offered a full refund, which I accepted. It is now May, and despite repeated assurances that the refund would be processed (on 8/4, 14/4, 24/4 and 27/4), I have received only one-third of the amount owed.

As both a children’s rights campaigner and an educational services business owner myself, I find this deeply concerning. Clear communication, transparency, and honouring agreed refunds are basic standards that any professional organisation should uphold.

After months of chasing by email and phone, with repeated promises but no resolution, I now feel I have no option other than to pursue legal action to recover the outstanding balance.

Based on my experience, I would urge others to exercise caution before making payment to this company.

Currently awaiting a response from their member services team. Would not recommend signing up until they sort out how they handle tier changes mid-contract.

Paid for multi-club access. They took it away overnight.

I joined Virgin Active specifically because my Multi Access membership gave me access to clubs near both my workplace and my family - specifically the Strand Branch is near my office. That was the whole point. Without it, the membership simply doesn't work for my life.

With no advance warning whatsoever, I received an email on 1st May telling me that three clubs - Strand, Crouch End and Clapham - had been moved to a higher tier, effective that same day. I have now lost access to all three, and when I contacted Virgin Active to discuss this, I was told the only resolution was to pay an additional £28 per month.

I find this deeply frustrating. The ability to access multiple clubs wasn't a perk - it was the entire basis on which I signed up and have been a member since July 2023. To have that significantly reduced overnight, with no notice period and no meaningful remedy offered, feels like a breach of the consumer rights I'm entitled to under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, which protects against businesses making unilateral changes that materially reduce the service a customer contracted for.

I will be making a formal complaint and I'm also seeking advice on my options. I'd encourage anyone considering a Multi Access membership to think carefully about whether Virgin Active will honour what you sign up for - because based on my experience, there is nothing stopping them from quietly reducing your access and asking you to pay more to get it back.

Based on my recent experience with Glen’s Virgin Active Strand club, the process showed a clear lack of communication and overall unprofessionalism.

For a brand positioning itself as premium, this is highly concerning and potentially damaging to business standards and reputation. In the early stages of leadership, especially within the first months in role, such issues can negatively impact the image of the brand — and in this case, that impact is already evident.

one_star_reviews.text:
Since my surgery with Mr. Brookes in 2017, I have been diagnosed with Secondary Atrophic Rhinitis (J31.0), a life-altering loss of nasal function that was never discussed as a risk.

I am writing this to provide a factual account of my long-term clinical outcome following FESS Major, Inferior Turbinate Reduction (Submucosal), and Septoplasty performed by Mr Gerald Brookes.

After enduring Nasal Trauma and a severe upper respiratory tract infection,  I had my sinuses cauterised 3 times on 9 June, 17 June, 11 October 2016.

I was advised to have my deviated septum straightened and my sinuses ‘opened up’ by Mr Gerald Brookes.

On 7th December 2017 I underwent Septoplasty (Code E0360), Reduction of Inferior Turbinates (Code E0412),  FESS Major (Code E1432) along with additional post-surgical cauterisation.

Since 2015 Montgomery Law requires clinics and surgeons to inform the prospective patients of the risks involved, such as Secondary Atrophic Rhintis & Empty Nose Syndrome. In my view, the informed consent process did not meet the Montgomery standards, as the specific risks of Secondary Atrophic Rhinitis were never discussed with me personally.

While Mr Brookes maintains that the "tissue-sparing" technique (submucosal reduction) cannot lead to complications, my post-operative reality has been diagnosed independently by specialists as Secondary Atrophic Rhinitis (ICD-10: J31.0) and Chronic Atrophic Mucosa.

The Clinical Reality: Since the procedure, I have suffered from a permanent loss of natural nasal moisture regulation.

My daily life now involves:

Constant Nasal Sluggishness: A sensation that the nasal "engine" has failed, where mucus stagnates rather than clearing.

Morning Crusts and Hemorrhaging: Waking up every morning with dry, clear flakes and streaks of blood—documented over several years across various climates.

Hypersensitivity: A raw, exposed sensation in the nasal passages that makes urban smells and pollutants physically irritating.

The Response: When I sought assistance regarding these life-altering symptoms, Mr Brookes dismissed the causality based on the surgical method used. However, the physical reality—confirmed by independent diagnostic imaging and clinical exams showing "wide nasal passages" and "atrophic lining"—contradicts the "success" of the surgery.

Advice for Patients: Be aware that "minimally invasive" or "submucosal" labels do not guarantee the preservation of nasal function. If you value your nasal physiology and wish to avoid a lifetime of saline rinses and lubricating gels to manage constant dryness, I strongly urge you to research the long-term risks of secondary atrophy (also referred to as Empty Nose Syndrome) and over-patency before proceeding.

I purchased a vehicle from this garage and opted for an extended warranty. Within one month of ownership, the engine management light and dashboard warnings illuminated. I brought the car back to the garage, where they replaced the oxygen sensor and cleared the diagnostic codes.
Unfortunately, the underlying issue was not resolved. Shortly after, the car began to experience severe performance issues, specifically heavy jerking and shuddering. This culminated in a frightening incident where the vehicle lost power while I was driving on a motorway, which created an extremely dangerous situation.
I am very disappointed to report that, due to the severity of these unresolved mechanical faults, the car is now beyond repair and has to be scrapped. I felt it was important to share my experience regarding the quality of the diagnosis and the subsequent impact on vehicle safety.

BLUF - Balham sold our, returned, broken car without our knowledge, despite refusing to refund us for it. A court ordered full payment including costs and hire car fees.

Balham Cars sold us a car which instantly developed issues, including the electronic handbrake not working. They advised us to drive the car back to them (despite knowing the extremely dangerous condition with no handbrake, and informing them this is impossible on the ferry as you have to vacate vehicles), and subsequently refused to arrange for the car to be fixed, even after a mechanic had identified the many issues; things which should have been identified and fixed before being sold. The AA identified the same issues on two occasions after being called out due to these issues stranding my partner at the side of the road. Of course, Balham claimed that mechanics and the AA were dodgy and in cohorts trying to drum up business for the mechanic - despite the mechanic advising he could work on it if we really wanted, but his strongly urged advice was to swiftly return the car as it shouldn't have been sold in this condition. An interesting business choice if they weren't just genuinely trying to help. They put all of this in writing, and all of it was in front of the judge and in the court documentation bundle.

More shockingly, after we returned the car to them at our own cost, they refused to issue a refund, and then ALSO sold the car to someone else, without consent or even notification, in fact their own take by email was that they were refusing to refund the car. I wonder what their approach would have been if we had chosen to collect the car at any point during this. They did not relay any money for the refund, so effectively sold our car.

We took them to court, where their own instructed barrister was as bewildered with Balham Cars as the Judge was, and to quote the court transcript, "I can think of no reason that the claimants should not get all they are asking for", which included all costs for initial mechanic assessment and fixes, and for returning the car, along with hire car costs for the entire duration we were without the vehicle.

The real concern of the situation is Vai's repeated arrogance, which is clear and on display in many of the negative reviews. In person whilst in court, it was very interesting to see how different and shell-shocked he was by the situation. Having no clear answer as to how it can ever be acceptable to not refund us, but especially after already reselling the car they were refusing to take. Consider the type of person that thinks this is an acceptable business practice. There is always an excuse or someone else to blame for issues. The Approved Judgement for this case is very interesting reading regarding the Judge's views on Balham Cars' business practices...

You can take a chance and hope nothing goes wrong with the car - but the negative reviews and more importantly the responses always blaming the other party should paint a very clear picture of how terribly issues are handled if you are do have any issues.

Update: To respond to Vai ignoring the truth again - the court documentation is available as he well knows - the court agreed with all costs, and the transcript is available if anyone wishes to verify. These are public orders and freely available - interesting (yet expected) approach to lie about this.

one_star_reviews.text:
I visited this store around two times beforehand, deliberately posing as a casual, less experienced buyer to get a genuine feel for how they treat customers. I work full-time in grading and regularly handle cards worth £1000+, so I was seriously considering building a long-term relationship here given the convenience of the location, and that soon I was moving to London.

Before visiting, one thing kept coming up when I spoke to other collectors at shows and meetups: concerns about a particular staff member. Multiple people mentioned poor attitude, making fun of customers inspecting cards, and peer pressuring to buy especially when customers questioned condition, and other mannerisms such as kissing teeth when asking to take a card out the case. I initially gave the benefit of the doubt, assuming maybe these were isolated incidents or misunderstandings.

Unfortunately, after my visits, I can confirm those concerns are completely valid.

Yakin (the owner, usually wearing glasses) is excellent. Professional, respectful, and clearly knows how to run things properly. However, the other staff member who is often beside him at the display case was consistently the opposite, and it significantly impacted my experience as he's the one managing the case.

During one visit, I asked to inspect a £40 card with grading in mind. His immediate response was dismissive and sarcastic, saying “it’s pack fresh bro, what do these people want,” before reluctantly letting me look at it. While I was inspecting the card, he made comments to another customer (who clearly was a friend glazing him) and openly mocked me, calling me a “jokeman” and saying I was “pissing him off” for simply checking the condition.

Within seconds, I identified a noticeable dent in the middle of the card, something that would significantly affect its grade. So not only was the attitude unprofessional, but it was also completely unjustified given the card clearly had issues.

This kind of behavior is unacceptable in a space where condition is everything, especially when dealing with serious collectors or graders. At the time, I had around £30k allocated for a bulk purchase and I wanted to spend £5k here (and went on to do so at other shops and shows over the course of my trip), but that interaction alone was enough for me to decide I won’t be doing business with this store again.

To be clear: Yakin is great, and I have no issues with him. But as long as that other staff member is representing the store, I won’t be returning, and for anyone else who is looking to deal in higher end singles or enjoys polite customer service, I suggest you do the same.

one_star_reviews.text:
Nothing personal to the doctor, he’s just doing his job. But this clinic paints everybody with EUPD with the same brush because of one court case where somebody sadly took their own life and the family blamed the cannabis. My own family also tries to blame my mental health on cannabis to avoid accountability for the environment I grew up in, despite the fact I was miserable and unproductive long before I ever smoked.

My sociability, appetite, productivity and sleep were all areas that improved massively with cannabis, the same way antidepressants work for some people and not others. It worked for me without me even feeling dependent on it. Personally, I believe stigma and shame around cannabis and mental health do far more damage than honest, regulated support.

If somebody was genuinely suffering severe side effects or psychosis from cannabis, then clearly there should have been better assessment and monitoring involved. That doesn’t mean every patient with EUPD is some unstable liar or incapable of responsible use.

I also find the inconsistency frustrating. Mental health conditions like depression, PTSD and anxiety are all associated with elevated suicide risk too, yet people with those diagnoses are not automatically treated like liabilities in the same way. It feels like EUPD patients are singled out because of stigma and public fear rather than nuanced individual assessment.

And the hypocrisy from wider society is exhausting. People are happy to judge cannabis users while heavily drinking alcohol or smoking cigarettes, despite the obvious health consequences associated with those substances too. Somehow cannabis users are still treated like irresponsible criminals regardless of whether they are functioning adults with jobs and stable lives.

What frustrates me most is that denying medical cannabis doesn’t magically stop people from using it. It just pushes people toward the street market instead of safe, regulated products. I approached this clinic hoping for clean, legal medical support rather than having to take risks elsewhere.

The policy feels incredibly backhanded and discriminatory. They seem happy to prescribe for certain mental health conditions but suddenly draw the line at EUPD because of fear and damage control. It reinforces the stigma that people with personality disorders are somehow dangerous or incapable of making informed decisions about their own treatment.

I’m a productive working adult who has never harmed anyone, and I found this whole experience deeply disappointing. I expected nuance and individual assessment, not blanket assumptions based on diagnosis labels.

DO NOT GO HERE! Completely Heartless and Unprofessional.

We brought our cat in after he had passed away a few weeks ago, and the way we were treated during one of the most painful moments of our lives was nothing short of appalling.

We were told to leave him in a room while the receptionist “discussed pricing” with us. Not a single word of compassion, no acknowledgment of our loss - just a pricing chart handed to us while we were visibly devastated. It felt cold, transactional, and completely devoid of empathy.

While my boyfriend and I were standing there crying, trying to speak to a receptionist, Zara (nurse) came into the room and stood extremely close to us - so close that we could hear everything clearly. There was no real attempt at discretion. She asked the receptionist which pet it was, and instead of speaking privately, the receptionist typed the name out on the computer right in front of us.

As soon as she realised, Zara reacted with visible relief and said, “what a relief… I thought it was—” referring to another pet. She then walked away without acknowledging us in any way.

We were completely stunned. This all happened within feet of us, while we were actively grieving. Hearing relief expressed in that moment - simply because it wasn’t a different case - made our loss feel completely dismissed and insignificant.

What makes this even worse is that she has seen our cat before. She knew us. Yet she didn’t say a single word to us, didn’t look at us, didn’t acknowledge our loss in any way. She came in purely to satisfy her own curiosity, reacted insensitively, and left.

The lack of professionalism, empathy, and basic human decency is staggering. This experience made an already devastating loss so much harder to bear.

Based on our experience - and seeing that others have had similar issues with Dr Saskia - we would strongly advise people to think twice before bringing their pets here. At a time when compassion should be the bare minimum, all we were shown was insensitivity and a clear focus on money over care.

After hearing positive things about Tom Austen as a podiatrist in the area, I made the decision to book at st Lawrence clinic to have a session.

The consultation itself was professional and thorough. He carried out a number of assessments, including looking at the way I walked and ran, which I appreciated. However, I ultimately came away feeling slightly disappointed, mainly because I was hoping for more clarity and guidance regarding my condition. While the session confirmed issues I was already aware of, I didn’t feel I received much explanation as to why these problems were happening or what long-term options were available to improve them which was my main reason to going.

I also felt that the main outcome of the appointment was being advised to purchase insoles. After already paying £80 for a 30-minute consultation, it was a little discouraging to then feel that the only real solution presented involved an additional £80 expense. I understand insoles can be beneficial, but I had hoped for a broader discussion around different treatment approaches, exercises, rehabilitation plans, or lifestyle adjustments that might help alongside them.

Another thing that added to my disappointment was that I was told I would receive a follow-up email around a month later to check on my progress and see whether the insoles were helping. Unfortunately, I never received any follow-up communication, which left me feeling overlooked after the appointment.

Overall, while the consultation was professional and the staff and clinic were nice, I left feeling no more informed or reassured about my condition than when I arrived. I had hoped for a more personalised experience and a clearer plan moving forward.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had a very disappointing experience dealing with this agency regarding a holding deposit for a room at 11A Lindley Street.

Before making payment, I specifically requested clarification and formal documentation regarding the holding deposit terms. No formal signed holding deposit agreement was provided beyond WhatsApp messages.

I was also initially quoted the wrong room price before later being told the actual figure was higher, which added to the confusion surrounding the arrangement and terms communicated prior to payment.

Most concerningly, I withdrew my interest less than an hour after making the payment, with both the payment and cancellation occurring outside company working hours. No tenancy agreement had been signed, I never moved into the property, and the tenancy process had barely progressed at the point of cancellation.

Despite this extremely short timeframe, the agency retained the full £205 holding deposit.

I attempted multiple times to resolve the matter amicably and professionally through email, including requesting clarification regarding what actual administrative work or financial loss justified retention of the full amount, but I did not receive a clear breakdown.

I would strongly advise future tenants to ensure they receive clear written documentation regarding holding deposit terms before making any payment and to proceed cautiously when dealing with non-refundable deposit arrangements.
